edelweiss_group.sector: Financial Services / Diversified NBFC & Wholesale Lending
edelweiss_group.exclusionReason: Severe Regulatory Supervisory Action: In May 2024, RBI imposed a supervisory ban on ECL Finance (cease & desist structured transactions/wholesale lending) and Edelweiss ARC (prohibited from acquiring financial assets/SRs) for evergreening stressed loans, circumventing regulations, and governance deficiencies.
edelweiss_group.detailedCaseHistory: In May 2024, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) issued landmark supervisory directions against ECL Finance Ltd and Edelweiss Asset Reconstruction Company Ltd (EARC). RBI found structured financial arrangements designed to evergreen stressed debt facilities and circumvent regulatory provisioning norms. ECL Finance was directed to cease and desist from undertaking structured transactions, while EARC was prohibited from acquiring financial assets. Additionally, group entities faced inquiries in 2023-2024 related to insolvency proceedings (e.g. Nitin Desai studio loan matter) and ED/CBI investigative scrutiny.
edelweiss_group.earlierBankruptciesOrDefaults: No direct technical NCD default, but multiple developer and corporate loans originated by ECL Finance underwent NCLT resolutions with substantial haircuts.
edelweiss_group.regulatoryActions: RBI Supervised Cease & Desist (May 2024) on ECL Finance wholesale transactions and EARC asset acquisitions; regular SEBI inspection observations.
edelweiss_group.auditorAndAccountingQuality: Audited by S.R. Batliboi & Co. and NGS & Co. LLP with emphasis of matter paragraphs regarding wholesale exposure provisions.
edelweiss_group.investmentVerdict: HIGH RISK / STRATEGIC EXIT: Substantial regulatory overhang, constrained wholesale liquidity, and ongoing business restructuring warrant strict exclusion from capital-preservation portfolios.
edelweiss_group.promoterJourney: Rashesh Shah co-founded Edelweiss Group in 1995 with Venkat Ramaswamy as an investment banking boutique, scaling it into a diversified financial powerhouse spanning NBFC lending, ARC, housing finance, insurance, and wealth management. Navigated 2008 GFC and 2018 IL&FS crisis. Led institutional demerger of Nuvama Wealth in 2023 with PAG Asia.

keertana_spandana.detailedCaseHistory: Padmaja Reddy founded Spandana Sphoorty and navigated it through the 2010 Andhra MFI crisis and CDR. In October 2021, she was abruptly forced to resign as Managing Director by the Board and PE investor Kedaara Capital following conflicts over a proposed sale to Axis Bank and corporate governance differences. Litigation and arbitration ensued regarding client data transfer and non-compete clauses. Subsequently, she launched Keertana Finserv in rural and semi-urban lending, expanding rapidly in Andhra, Telangana, and Odisha.
keertana_spandana.earlierBankruptciesOrDefaults: Spandana underwent Corporate Debt Restructuring (CDR) during the 2010 AP MFI crisis and successfully exited in 2017 with full repayment.

keertana_spandana.auditorAndAccountingQuality: Audited by B S R & Associates / Walker Chandiok with standard microfinance portfolio aging and ECL provisions.
keertana_spandana.investmentVerdict: HIGH RISK: Sub-A rating (IND BBB+), promoter track record of boardroom friction with institutional PE, and unsecured rural exposure require mandatory exclusion from conservative portfolios.
keertana_spandana.promoterJourney: Padmaja Reddy pioneered microfinance in Andhra Pradesh founding Spandana Sphoorty in 1998, surviving the 2010 AP MFI crisis and successfully engineering CDR exit and IPO. Following board disputes with Kedaara Capital in 2021, she founded Keertana Finserv in 2022, rapidly scaling a high-touch rural lending operation across 8 Indian states.
